items.event_time_ist: Wednesday morning, Oct 21, 2026 (exact time undetermined; reported by Arab News ~8:04 AM local)
items.source_name: Al Jazeera / Al-Arabiya via Arab News / Jamaican Inquirer
items.summary: A powerful explosion was heard in Aden on Wednesday morning and smoke was seen rising near Aden International Airport, confirmed by an Al Jazeera journalist, a Yemeni police official, and an Al-Arabiya correspondent (Al-Arabiya says the missile struck the airport runway). Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree claimed responsibility, saying the group targeted the Saudi-led coalition's 'military operation room at the Badr Camp in Aden with a ballistic missile,' describing the strike as 'precise and direct.' The target/damage claim is Houthi-sourced and unverified; no casualty figures have been reported. This follows Friday's Aden airport attack (two missiles on airport grounds, no casualties), making this at least the third such strike on the facility.
items.title: Houthi ballistic missile strikes Aden airport area Wednesday; explosion heard, smoke rising

items.event_time_ist: Wednesday, Oct 21, 2026 (statement reported ~9:45 AM UTC / 3:15 PM IST)
items.summary: Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said Wednesday the group launched no drones toward the Saudi holy city of Medina and conducted no military operations toward Saudi Arabia at all, denying earlier coalition statements that it had intercepted drones over Medina and the Eastern region (intercepts already tracked in the timeline's multi-region-interceptions item). The denial is carried only as Reuters wire copy so far; no second independent outlet has picked it up with original reporting, so it remains single-sourced.
items.title: Saree denies any Wednesday drone launches toward Medina or Saudi Arabia, disputing coalition intercept claims
